clue.text: In charge of backing een-tres

indicators.note: backing tells us to run the pieces before it from back to front

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A supporter of some unnamed venues takes charge of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns the whole two-piece run, not just one piece. 'centres' is the plural of the definition word, matching the Latin plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Foci are focal points, places where activity gathers, the plural of focus.

clue.text: Part of plane has safety device to limit wind blowing up

indicators.note: to limit means the outer word bounds and encloses the next piece

parts.note: a fuse is an electrical safety device

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

explanation.surface: An aircraft carries a device to stop wind gusting upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'blowing up' reads the wind word from the bottom, and 'to limit' means the safety device encloses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuselage is the main body of an aircraft, carrying crew and passengers.

clue.text: American primary?

parts.note: looks like a US election contest, but means red, blue or yellow spelt the US way

explanation.definitionFit: The US spelling drops the u, and red, blue and yellow are the primary hues.

clue.text: With no charge for delivery?

parts.note: reads like free postage, but describes a person who came into the world as a citizen rather than a slave

explanation.definitionFit: A person of free birth was delivered, at birth, without the legal burden of servitude.

clue.text: Organise staple food in Cheshire place

parts.note: to run something is to organise it
corn is a staple grain

explanation.surface: Someone sets up a supply of basic grain in an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheshire is a county in north-west England; Runcorn is a town there.
explanation.definitionFit: Runcorn is an industrial town on the Mersey in that county.

clue.text: Choose artist's buildings to describe daughter's psychological problem

parts.note: to elect is to choose
RA, Royal Academician, is a crossword artist; the 's is a link
a complex is a group of buildings

explanation.surface: Picking out a painter's buildings, a therapist describes a daughter's troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jung's theory, a girl's rivalry with her mother for her father's love is the female counterpart of the Oedipus complex.

clue.text: Having some idea colic could result from tart substance

indicators.note: could result says the letters may be reworked into a different order

explanation.surface: A tart could cause stomach pain, if one has the faintest notion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could result' rearranges the nine letters of IDEA COLIC. 'tart' means sour, the property of an acid.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fatty acid found in olive oil; tartness is the sharp taste of acids generally.

clue.text: Cause confusion over bananas?

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: to stun is to daze or bewilder

explanation.surface: Fruit causes mix-ups.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are slang for crazy or mad.

clue.text: Factory workers who dislike modern technology?

definitions.meaning: operatives who tend machines in a factory
people who object to machines, taking mind in its sense of resent

explanation.definitionFit: Factory hands tend engines, and anyone who objects to mechanisation could also be said to mind them.

clue.text: Woman in army vetted

indicators.note: in tells us the name sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A woman joining the military was screened first.
explanation.definitionFit: Yvette is a woman's given name, of French origin.

clue.text: Pushiness of fellow in organising Candlemas event

indicators.note: organising means putting the letters of the fodder into a new order

explanation.surface: A pushy man takes charge of the arrangements for a church festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organising' rearranges F with CANDLEMAS and EVENT, fifteen letters in all. Candlemas is a Christian feast on 2 February.
explanation.definitionFit: Promoting oneself aggressively is a form of pushy ambition.

clue.text: Movement of divine type to disadvantaged quarter

parts.note: a Lar is a Roman household god, one of the Lares
a ghetto is a deprived district of a city

explanation.surface: A clergyman is sent to work in a poor part of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' suggests a clergyman, but here it is a god: the Roman household spirit Lar.
explanation.definitionFit: Larghetto marks a section of a symphony or sonata played fairly slowly, and such a section is called a movement.

clue.text: Friar having adjustment to make garment smaller?

definitions.meaning: Friar ... is the jovial monk of the Robin Hood legends
a stitched fold taken in to shorten or narrow clothing

explanation.definitionFit: The outlaw band's monk bears this name, and dressmakers use the same word for a sewn fold that takes clothing in.

clue.text: Greek woman who has secondary issue?

parts.note: Annie is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A Greek lady has a problem of minor importance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' means offspring: grandchildren are the second generation of issue, hence 'secondary'.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandmother has grandchildren, her children's offspring, descendants once removed.

clue.text: A laboratory flower in stone

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like flower

explanation.surface: A lab keeps a flower set in stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a fine translucent mineral carved for ornaments.

clue.text: Sister joining Church of England retains a particular shade of meaning

indicators.note: retains means the joined pieces hold the next letter within them

parts.note: a sister in a religious order is a nun

explanation.surface: A nun who joins the established church keeps a subtle distinction in her views.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a subtle difference in sense or tone.

clue.text: Remodelled Sun should be not wanted

indicators.note: remodelled means the next word's letters are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: ought means should

explanation.surface: A newspaper being redesigned should not be wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remodelled' rearranges SUN to give UNS. 'Sun' looks like the British tabloid, but it is just the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not sought is unrequested or unwelcome.

clue.text: Old feast of Latin American mothers

parts.note: mas are mothers, informally

explanation.surface: A traditional celebration is held by Hispanic mums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin American' looks like one phrase but supplies two abbreviations. Lammas (1 August) was the old English harvest festival of loaf-mass.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a harvest festival in the medieval English church year, celebrated on 1 August.

clue.text: Awful person also has to be restricted by moderate

indicators.note: to be restricted by means the piece before is held within the next one

parts.note: so-so means moderate, middling
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A nasty man has also been kept in check by someone of moderate views.
explanation.definitionFit: So-and-so is a euphemism for an unpleasant or contemptible person.

clue.text: Left standing apart in marshy land in battle

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the marsh word that follows

parts.note: a fen is low marshy ground
odd means unmatched, standing apart from a pair

explanation.surface: A soldier left alone in a bog during the fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: Flodden (1513) was a battle in Northumberland in which the English defeated the Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Flodden Field is the site of a famous English victory over James IV of Scotland.

clue.text: Woman who could make a fit Ma?

indicators.note: could make says these letters can be reworked into another form

explanation.surface: Which woman might turn into a healthy mother?
explanation.definitionFit: Fatima is a woman's name, borne by the daughter of the Prophet Muhammad.

clue.text: Futile one's in the lead

indicators.note: in puts the letter for one within the word for the lead

parts.note: the van is the leading part of an army or procession
one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: Someone at the front reckons it is a pointless position.
explanation.definitionFit: Efforts made in vain are pointless and achieve nothing.

clue.text: Against history of course

parts.note: anti means against
the past is history
o' is a shortened form of of, as in o'clock

explanation.surface: Someone protests against the history taught on a programme of study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests a programme of study, but it is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian starter served before the main dishes is one part of a meal.

clue.text: Thus employ soak

parts.note: so means thus
to use is to employ

explanation.surface: In this way, put a drunkard to work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soak' looks like a noun for a heavy drinker, as is souse, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To souse is to drench or steep something in liquid.

clue.text: Oath for example by a daughter

explanation.surface: A father swears, for instance, by his daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Egad is an archaic mild exclamation, a minced form of by God.

clue.text: Arranging unmortgaged term which entertains Germans at great length

definitions.text: which entertains Germans at great length

indicators.note: arranging puts the letters of the two words into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone sorting out a mortgage-free term finds the Germans enjoy a long show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranging' rearranges the fifteen letters of UNMORTGAGED and TERM.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's last Ring opera runs for over four hours, a famously long German night at the opera.

clue.text: The German is to charge for mockery

parts.note: der is a German word for the
taken as written
an ion is an atom carrying an electric charge

explanation.surface: A German man is about to charge someone with mockery.
explanation.definitionFit: Scornful ridicule and contempt amount to the same thing.

clue.text: Throw stones and hide

definitions.meaning: an animal's skin with its fur

explanation.definitionFit: Pelting is hurling things at a target, and a pelt is an animal skin with fur.
